source_text:
ἐπεὶ οὖν τὰ προσωποποιηθέντα ῥήματα οὔτε τῷ θεσπεσίῳ Παύλῳ ἁρμόζει, οὔτε μὴν παντὶ τῷ συνταφέντι Χριστῷ διὰ τοῦ βαπτίσματος, διότι τῆς ὀνομαζομένης σαρκὸς ἠλευθερώθησαν· οὐ γὰρ ἔτι κατακριθήσονται οἱ τοιοῦτοι διὰ τὴν τοῦ Ἀδὰμ παρακοήν, οὐκέτι βασιλεύει αὐτῶν ἡ ἁμαρτία, οὐχ ὁ θάνατος ὁ διὰ τῆς ἁμαρτίας· συνετάφησαν γὰρ τῇ ζωῇ τοῦ Χριστοῦ διὰ τῆς ὑπακοῆς τὴν παρακοὴν
ἐξαφανίσαντος, καὶ τῷ ἑκουσίῳ ἑαυτοῦ θανάτῳ τὸν ἐξ αὐτῆς ἐπισυμβάντα ἡμῖν θάνατον ἐκκρουσαμένῳ· γέγονε γὰρ ἑκὼν ὑπὸ νόμον τὸν τῆς παρακοῆς, ἵνα ἡμᾶς 1 τοὺς ὑπὸ νόμον τὸν τῆς κατακρίσεως ἐξαγοράσῃ. διὰ τοῦτο ἔφη πᾶς λελυτρωμένος· χάρις δὲ τῷ θεῷ διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν· τὸ γὰρ ἀδύνατον τοῦ νόμου, ἐν ᾧ ἠσθένει διὰ τῆς σαρκός, ὁ θεὸς τὸν ἑαυτοῦ υἱὸν πέμψας ἐν ὁμοιώματι σαρκὸς ἁμαρτίας, κατέκρινε τὴν ἁμαρτίαν ἐν τῇ σαρκί. ὅτι δὲ ταῦθ' οὕτω καλῶς τεθεώρηται, ἐπιφέρει λέγων ὁ θεῖος ἀπόστολος· οὐδὲν ἄρα κατάκριμα τοῖς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ· ὁ γὰρ νόμος τοῦ πνεύματος τῆς ζωῆς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ ἠλευθέρωσέν με ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου τῆς ἁμαρτίας καὶ τοῦ θανάτου, καὶ τὰ τούτων ἑξῆς. 3 Πειράσω δὴ διὰ βραχέων καὶ εἰς αὐτὰ τὰ ῥήματα τὰ κατὰ προσωποποιΐαν εἰρημένα παρατρεχόντως εἰπεῖν, ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀφορμὴν δὲ λαβοῦσα ἡ ἁμαρτία διὰ τῆς ἐντολῆς ἐξηπάτησεν με καὶ δι' αὐτῆς ἀπέκτεινεν. Τὸ ἁμαρτίας ὄνομα οὐκ οὐσίαν ὑφεστῶσαν δηλοῖ, ἀλλὰ τρόπον καὶ βίον τοῦ διημαρτηκέναι τινὰ τοῦ κατὰ λόγον καὶ ὀρθῶς ἔχοντος πράγματος· ὥσπερ γὰρ γενικώτατόν ἐστιν ὄνομα ἡ ἁμαρτία, κατὰ πολλῶν καὶ διαφόρων πραγμάτων κατηγορουμένη. πᾶν δὲ ἁμάρτημα οὔτε λόγῳ οὔτε νόμῳ προστακτικῷ γίνεται· εἰ γὰρ κατὰ νόμον καὶ λόγον ἐγίνετο ὀρθόν, οὐκέτι ἂν ἦν ἁμάρτημα ὡρισμένον καὶ τεταγμένον ἔχον τὸν τῆς γενέσεως λόγον. ἐπειδὴ δὲ ὁ θεῖος ἀπόστολος οὐχ ἁπλῶς ἁμαρτημάτων, ἀλλ' ἁμαρτίας γενικωτάτης ἐχούσης φρόνημα, ἐχούσης νόμον, δυναμένης σοφίσασθαι, ἀφορμὰς πορίσασθαι πρὸς τὴν τοῦ κακοῦ κατασκευὴν μνημονεύει, οὐκ ἄλλον τινὰ γενικωτάτως ἁμαρτίαν ὀνομάζει, ἀλλ' ἢ αὐτὸν τὸν τῶν ἁμαρτημάτων ἀρχηγέτην καὶ πατέρα διάβολον. ὅτου χάριν καὶ βασιλεύειν τῶν ἁμαρτημάτων αὐτὸν ὁ ἀπόστολος ἀπεφήνατο· μὴ οὖν βασιλευέτω ἡ ἁμαρτία ἐν τῷ θνητῷ ὑμῶν σώματι. ὡς γὰρ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ἀφ' ἧς ἐπιτηδεύουσι τέχνης καλοῦμεν, οὕτω δὴ καὶ αὐτὸν τὸν διάβολον ὡς πρώτως ἐφευρετὴν γενόμενον τῆς ἁμαρτίας, ἁμαρτίαν καλεῖ. Ἐπειδὴ τοίνυν διὰ τῆς δοθείσης τῷ Ἀδὰμ ἐντολῆς τὸν ἄνθρωπον ἠπάτησεν, καὶ δι' αὐτῆς τὸν Ἀδάμ, ἀφορμὰς πορισάμενος διὰ τῆς ἐντολῆς. ἔστι δὲ αὕτη· τί ὅτι, φησίν, εἶπεν ὁ θεός· ἀπὸ παντὸς ξύλου τοῦ ἐν τῷ παραδείσῳ οὐ φάγεσθε βρώσει; καὶ ᾗ δ' ἂν ἡμέρᾳ φάγησθε ἀπ' αὐτοῦ, διανοιχθήσονται ὑμῶν οἱ ὀφθαλμοί, καὶ ἔσεσθε ὡς θεοί, γινώσκοντες καλὸν καὶ πονηρόν. σοφίζεται δὲ αὐτοὺς μείζονι ἐπαγγελίᾳ κατακρύψαι τὴν ἀπάτην, ὑπισχνεῖται τὸ πλέον, ἵνα τοὺς τῆς ἐντολῆς φύλακας τῶν τῆς ἀρετῆς βάθρων τῷ ὁμοίῳ αὐτοὺς πτώματι καταστρέψῃ· τὸν γὰρ ἄνθρωπον ἐξοιστρήσας ἴσα θεῷ ἐθέλειν γενέσθαι, τῆς κατ' ἀπάτην ὁμιλίας τὴν ἀφορμὴν ἐπορίζετο ἐκ τῆς παρασχεθείσης ἐντολῆς. ὅτου χάριν ὁ Παῦλος ἔφη· ἀφορμὴν δὲ λαβοῦσα ἡ ἁμαρτία διὰ τῆς ἐντολῆς ἐξηπάτησέν με.
thought_title: The substituted words fit no one buried with Christ; sin is the devil
orientation: Didymus has just shown that the words of Romans 7 cannot belong to Paul or any Christian, and now he explains why: those buried with Christ are freed from the flesh, sin, and death, and the 'sin' that deceived through the commandment is the devil himself.
pass_a_gloss: Since therefore the words spoken in character fit neither the inspired Paul, nor indeed every person buried with Christ through baptism, because they have been freed from the so-called flesh; for such people will no longer be condemned because of the disobedience of Adam, sin no longer reigns over them, nor death which is through sin; for they were buried together with the life of Christ, who through obedience obliterated the disobedience, and by his voluntary death drove out the death that came upon us from it; for he willingly came under the law of disobedience, in order that he might redeem us who are under the law of condemnation. For this reason every redeemed person said: but thanks be to God through Jesus Christ our Lord; for the impossibility of the law, in which it was weak through the flesh, God, having sent his own Son in the likeness of flesh of sin, condemned sin in the flesh. And that these things have been rightly viewed in this way, the inspired apostle adds, saying: there is therefore no condemnation for those in Christ Jesus; for the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has freed me from the law of sin and of death, and the things following these. I will attempt indeed through brief remarks to speak also about the very words spoken according to speaking in character, running through them, beginning from 'but sin, having taken an occasion through the commandment, deceived me and through it killed me.' The name of sin does not indicate a substance that exists, but a manner and way of life of someone having missed the mark of the matter that is according to reason and right; for just as sin is a most general name, being predicated of many and different matters. And every sin comes about neither by reason nor by a commanding law; for if it came about according to law and right reason, it would no longer be a sin having a defined and ordered principle of its coming into being. But since the inspired apostle mentions not simply sins, but a most general sin having a mind, having a law, being able to act craftily, to procure occasions for the construction of evil, he names no other as sin in the most general sense, but the very originator and father of sins, the devil. For which reason the apostle also declared that he reigns over sins: therefore do not let sin reign in your mortal body. For just as we call people by the craft which they practice, so indeed he also calls the devil himself sin, as having become the first inventor of sin. Since therefore through the commandment given to Adam he deceived the human being, and through it deceived Adam, having procured occasions through the commandment. And this is it: why is it, he says, that God said: you shall not eat by eating from every tree in the garden? And on whatever day you eat from it, your eyes will be opened, and you will be as gods, knowing good and evil. And he acts craftily toward them by a greater promise to conceal the deception, he promises the more, in order that he might overturn the guardians of the commandment from the foundations of virtue by a fall like his own; for having goaded the human being to want to become equal to God, he procured the occasion of the deceptive conversation from the commandment that had been given. For which reason Paul said: but sin, having taken an occasion through the commandment, deceived me.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'speaking in character' for προσωποποιΐα; the passive participle here means words that have been put into a character's mouth.
rejected: the words spoken in a role

choices.why: The participle ὀνομαζομένης signals that 'flesh' is a name, not the physical body; 'so-called' preserves the distancing force.

choices.term: τὸν ἐξ αὐτῆς ἐπισυμβάντα ἡμῖν θάνατον
choices.english: the death that came upon us from it
choices.why: ἐπισυμβάντα means 'happening upon' or 'befalling'; 'came upon us' keeps the sense of death as an event that overtook humanity from disobedience.
rejected: the death that resulted from it
the death that followed from it

choices.english: a most general sin having a mind
choices.why: γενικωτάτης is superlative of 'general,' and φρόνημα means a mind or way of thinking; the phrase personifies sin as a thinking agent, which Didymus identifies as the devil.
rejected: a most generic sin having a mindset
a most general sin having a thought

choices.english: by a fall like his own
choices.why: The dative πτώματι is instrumental, and ὁμοίῳ refers to the devil's own fall; 'his own' makes clear the fall is the devil's, not the guardians'.

choices.term: ἀφορμὴν δὲ λαβοῦσα ἡ ἁμαρτία διὰ τῆς ἐντολῆς ἐξηπάτησέν με
choices.english: but sin, having taken an occasion through the commandment, deceived me
choices.why: This is the Pauline quotation Didymus is expounding; the rendering keeps the participle 'having taken' and the instrumental 'through the commandment' to match the source's syntax.
rejected: but sin, seizing an opportunity through the commandment, deceived me
but sin, taking occasion by the commandment, deceived me

pass_b_english: Since, then, the words spoken in character fit neither the inspired Paul nor anyone buried together with Christ through baptism—because such people have been freed from the so-called flesh—for such people will no longer be condemned because of Adam's disobedience; sin no longer reigns over them, nor the death that comes through sin. For they were buried together with the life of Christ, who obliterated disobedience by his obedience and drove out the death that came upon us from it by his voluntary death. For he willingly came under the law of disobedience, so that he might redeem us who were under the law of condemnation. For this reason every redeemed person says: “Thanks be to God through Jesus Christ our Lord” (Romans 7:25). For what the law could not do, weakened as it was through the flesh, God did by sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and he condemned sin in the flesh (Romans 8:3).

That these things have been rightly understood in this way, the divine apostle shows by adding: “There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus. For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has set me free from the law of sin and death” (Romans 8:1-2), and what follows these words.

Let me now attempt, briefly and in passing, to speak about the very words spoken in character, beginning from “But sin, having taken an occasion through the commandment, deceived me and through it killed me” (Romans 7:11). The name “sin” does not indicate a subsisting essence, but rather a manner and way of life of someone who has missed the mark of what is reasonable and right. For “sin” is a most general name, predicated of many different things. But every sin comes about neither by reason nor by a commanding law; for if it came about according to law and right reason, it would no longer be a sin, since it would have a defined and ordered principle of its coming into being.

Since, however, the divine apostle does not mention mere sins, but a most general sin having a mind, having a law, able to act craftily and to procure occasions for the construction of evil, he calls no other by the general name of sin than the originator and father of sins himself, the devil. For this reason the apostle also declared that he reigns over sins: “Therefore do not let sin reign in your mortal body” (Romans 6:12). For just as we call people by the craft they practice, so also he calls the devil himself “sin,” since he was the first inventor of sin.

Since, then, through the commandment given to Adam he deceived the man, and through it deceived Adam, procuring occasions through the commandment—and this is what he says: “Why is it that God said, ‘You shall not eat from any tree in the garden’? And on whatever day you eat from it, your eyes will be opened, and you will be like gods, knowing good and evil” (Genesis 3:1, 5). He acts craftily, hiding the deception under a greater promise; he promises more, so that he may overturn the guardians of the commandment from the foundations of virtue by a fall like his own. For having goaded the man to want to become equal to God, he procured the occasion for his deceptive conversation from the commandment that had been given. For this reason Paul said: “But sin, having taken an occasion through the commandment, deceived me.”

last_rejected.why: The Greek is "flesh of sin" (genitive), not "sinful flesh." The English "sinful flesh" suggests the flesh itself is sinful by nature, but Didymus's whole argument is that "sin" means the devil, not that the flesh is inherently sinful. "Flesh of sin" or "sin's flesh" would better preserve the personification. This misrepresents Didymus's theology.
last_rejected.fix: in the likeness of flesh of sin
last_rejected.ruling: σαρκὸς ἁμαρτίας is standard Pauline idiom; 'sinful flesh' is the conventional rendering and within normal range.

last_rejected.why: "Mind" is too neutral; φρόνημα here means a mindset, purpose, or willful intention—almost a hostile plan. "Having a purpose" or "with a will" better captures that this "sin" (the devil) has deliberate, scheming intentionality, not merely "a mind."
last_rejected.ruling: φρόνημα means mind/set/purpose; 'mind' is within normal range. Preference, not error.

last_rejected.why: "Construction" is awkward and misleading. κατασκευή here means preparation, arrangement, or contrivance of evil—scheming to bring evil about. "Construction" suggests building something physical. "Contrivance" or "preparation" better captures the devil's scheming.
last_rejected.ruling: κατασκευήν can mean construction/preparation/contrivance; 'construction' is within normal range.

last_rejected.why: "First inventor" is awkward; ἐφευρετής means discoverer, contriver, or deviser—someone who finds or schemes out something. "First contriver" or "originator" (already used earlier) would be better. "Inventor" has modern connotations of mechanical invention that mislead.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐφευρετής means inventor/discoverer/contriver; 'inventor' is within normal range.

last_rejected.quote: hiding the deception under a greater promise
last_rejected.why: "Under" is wrong; the dative μείζονι ἐπαγγελίᾳ means "by means of" or "with" a greater promise—he uses the greater promise as the tool to hide the deception. "Under" suggests the promise is a cover beneath which the deception lurks, which is close but not precise. "Behind a greater promise" or "using a greater promise to hide" would be clearer.
last_rejected.fix: hiding the deception behind a greater promise
last_rejected.ruling: Dative with κατακρύψαι can mean 'under'; rendering is within normal range, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.why: "Guardians" suggests official protectors; φύλακες here simply means "keepers" or "observers" of the commandment—those who keep/obey it. "Keepers of the commandment" is the standard English idiom.
last_rejected.ruling: φύλαξ means guardian/keeper; 'guardian' is within normal range. Mere preference.

last_rejected.quote: by a fall like his own
last_rejected.why: The Greek says "by a fall like his" (the devil's fall), but "his own" in English could ambiguously refer to the guardians' own fall. The point is the devil causes them to fall as he himself fell. "By a fall like his" would be clearer.
last_rejected.ruling: 'His own' refers contextually to the devil; no real ambiguity that misleads a careful reader.

last_rejected.why: ἐξοιστράω means to drive mad, frenzy, or madden—literally to sting or goad into madness. "Goaded" captures the physical action but loses the crucial sense of driving to frenzy/insanity. "Maddening" or "driving to frenzy" preserves the psychological violence.
last_rejected.fix: having driven the man to frenzy
last_rejected.ruling: ἐξοιστράω means goad/madden; 'goaded' is within normal range. Preference, not error.

last_rejected.why: ὁμιλία means intercourse, association, or conversation—here the devil's deceptive dealing/intercourse with Adam. "Conversation" is too weak and modern; "intercourse" (in older sense) or "dealings" better captures the intimate, corrupting interaction.
last_rejected.fix: the occasion for his deceptive dealings
last_rejected.ruling: ὁμιλία means conversation/intercourse/association; 'conversation' is within normal range.
